analysis:
Reviewed the docs-only change to docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. It adds an 'Add-on hold busy fields' section (head lines ~171-195), two new table rows (register ~284 and heartbeat ~383), and adds `addon_hold` to the model-autopilot busy-reason vocabulary (~1445). It also bumps the 'Last updated' date. No code or runtime behavior is changed in the supplied evidence.

Security-relevant contract described: while a local add-on holds the Mac, the provider stays registered and sends heartbeat.status=draining with optional busy_reason/busy_since_ms/busy_addon. A hold deliberately does not send provider_drain, so it does not fence the connection. Draining heartbeats already exclude routing at the coordinator (base line 345), and idle/serving clears the mark. The docs state that a coordinator ignoring the new fields still stops routing on the draining status. They also state that routed requests arriving during a hold get the typed draining rejection. This is consistent with the existing drain semantics (T-053 stale-authorization concern, TB-002) and does not extend authorization, App Attest proof lifetime, or serving permission. The fields are provider-self-reported, untrusted diagnostics: busy_addon is a free-form code-signing identifier string, and the docs describe no bound on its length or character set. Coordinator-side handling (length bound, sanitization for logs/console, and its use only as diagnostic and never for authorization) is platform-owned and outside the supplied evidence. This is a possible integration question, not a demonstrated regression. Also, a malicious provider could abuse draining to withhold capacity, but that is already self-controllable (ADV-001) and not new.

Unverified: the referenced implementation files (ProviderBusy.swift, CoordinatorClient+Registration.swift, ProtocolCodec.swift) and ../architecture/addon-hold.md are not in the supplied evidence. Whether register-with-busy preserves raw-attestation signature bytes, and whether the add-on hold authority is access-controlled locally, cannot be checked from this docs diff. The T-041 and prefix-cache content is unchanged context.
